passage.excerpt: Those called Ebionites agree that the world was made by God; but their opinions with respect to the Lord are similar to those of Cerinthus and Carpocrates. They use the Gospel according to Matthew only, and repudiate the Apostle Paul, maintaining that he was an apostate from the law. As regards the prophetical writings, they endeavour to interpret them in a singular manner. They practise circumcision and observe the Mosaic law. They affirm Jesus was the son of Joseph and Mary.

passage.excerpt: A certain Cerinthus in Asia taught that the world was not made by the primary God, but by a Power far separated from him and ignorant of the supreme authority. He maintained that Jesus was not born of a virgin, but was the son of Joseph and Mary according to the ordinary course of human generation. After baptism, Christ descended upon him in the form of a dove from the Supreme Ruler; then he proclaimed the unknown Father and performed miracles. But at last Christ departed from Jesus, and then Jesus suffered and rose again.

passage.notes: Bodily resurrection affirmed; Creator God as guarantee of resurrection; anti-materialist argument

passage.excerpt: God, then, having his own Word internal within his own bowels, begat him, emitting him along with his own wisdom before all things. He had this Word as a helper in the things that were created by him, and by him he made all things. He is called governing principle because he rules and is lord of all things fashioned by him.
passage.notes: Logos begotten from God before creation; Logos as helper and ruler of creation; pre-Nicene Logos theology
